title: Multiple Choice
instructions: Reminder: data sizes increase from byte to KB to MB to GB to TB. The build process goes from source code to compiler to assembler to linker, producing an executable. When a game launches, its executable moves from storage to RAM, then instructions move into cache for the CPU.

prompts.question: Which ordering lists these data sizes from SMALLEST to LARGEST?
What is the correct order of the build process, from source code to a runnable program?
answers: Write source code, compiler turns it into assembly, assembler turns it into object code, linker connects object files into an executable
Write source code, linker connects object files, compiler turns it into assembly, assembler creates the executable
Assembler creates object code, write source code, linker connects object files, compiler creates the executable
Compiler creates the executable, assembler turns it into source code, write source code, linker connects object files
prompts.correct_answer: Write source code, compiler turns it into assembly, assembler turns it into object code, linker connects object files into an executable

prompts.question: What is the final output of the build process called, the thing you can actually run?
What is the correct order when you launch a game?
answers: The executable sits in storage, it is loaded into RAM, instructions load from RAM into cache, and the CPU uses registers to carry out the instructions
The executable sits in storage, the CPU uses registers, it is loaded into RAM, and instructions load into cache
Instructions load into cache, the executable sits in storage, it is loaded into RAM, and the CPU uses registers
The executable is loaded into RAM, it sits in storage, the CPU uses registers, and instructions load into cache
prompts.correct_answer: The executable sits in storage, it is loaded into RAM, instructions load from RAM into cache, and the CPU uses registers to carry out the instructions
